title: Small-group recordings under Ellington sidemen's names
summary: Sessions credited to Sonny Greer and His Memphis Men, Barney and His Stinkopatsers or Rex Stewart's Rextet used Duke's players under other names because Duke was under contract.

bands.name: Sonny Greer and His Memphis Men
Harry Carney and His Big Eight

blocks.x: There were units, small units of the band sort of making their own recordings.
Oh, that came later.
That was from what year?
I don't remember.
Rex was the leader on one, Sonny Greer, Harry. You had --
I had one.
Did Duke play piano on all those?
Harry Carney didn't have any.
I have a record of 'Sleepy Baboon,' Harry Carney and his big eight.
Oh, I never heard of that one. That was after I left --
I think --
-- because I know --
-- that's the one with Harry. Or maybe that's Sonny Greer. I think that's Harry's.

Did Duke play piano on all of these --
Yeah, Duke.
-- or were they somebody else? But under another name usually, right?
Yeah. That was under our names, see. That's why they made it.
But I saw a list of personnel on several of them, on the label.

But it doesn't mean nothing. As long as whose group, the name of the group, you see. Because Duke was under contract with -- I don't know, at that time it might have been RCA or Victor or whatever.
